title: Workload Edge-Case Habitat and Probe Synthesis Cookbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview:
This cookbook defines a repeatable, low-friction process for discovering, synthesizing, and stewarding probe artifacts that exercise the long tail and brittle edge cases in production LLM workloads. It bridges prompt set generation, eval-harness ingestion, model-onboarding acceptance criteria, quantization sensitivity checks, and regression triage handoffs.

Why this exists:
- Edge-case failures are low-frequency but high-impact for user experience and downstream regressions.
- Synthesized probes enable safe, private, and repeatable stress-testing without exposing customer data.
- A single source-of-truth for probe format and telemetry makes downstream tooling (evaluators, alerting, rollback) deterministic.

Scope:
- Applies to: interactive chat, reranking, few-shot instruction-following, functioncall-heavy flows.
- Not covered: image-only or strictly offline batch embedding workloads (see separate multimodal playbooks).

Definitions:
- Probe: a single input + metadata + expected-signal set designed to exercise a behavior slice.
- Habitat: the contextual envelope (user persona, system prompt, long context, latency constraints) in which a probe is valid.
- Synthesizer: the process (automated or human-in-loop) that generates probes from seeds.
- Probe Manifest: canonical table of probes, ownership, and lifecycle state.

High-level workflow (summary):
1) Threat model & slice definition (owner: product/ML writer)
2) Seed collection (real traffic + adversarial templates)
3) Synthesis pass (automated paraphrase, noise injection, context morphing)
4) Filtering & tagging (sanitization, privacy gating)
5) Telemetry annotation and ingestion contract creation
6) Eval-harness ingestion and tiered prioritization
7) Onboarding acceptance checks (quant, latency, coherence)
8) Regression triage hooks and escalation mapping

Detailed steps: 
1) Threat model & slice definition
- Output: 1-page slice brief with a hypothesis, impact statement, and acceptance SLI. Example SLI: "semantic-preservation@95p >= 0.92 on 1k probes".
- Required fields: owner, use-case, primary model family affected, example failure modes.

2) Seed collection
- Inputs: anonymized production examples (if available), customer-reported tickets, synthetic adversarial templates from security team.
- Minimum seed size: 200 unique examples per high-priority slice, 50 for exploratory slices.

3) Synthesis pass (automated stages)
- Paraphrase generation: beam paraphrase with edit-distance threshold > 6 tokens.
- Noise injection: punctuation removal, repeated tokens, unicode confusables, code-switching (probability 0.12).
- Context morphing: move relevant history earlier/later; insert benign distractor turns.
- For functioncall services: vary function argument order, type coercion ("42" vs 42), and missing optional keys.
- Output: candidate probes with provenance tags (synth_tool:v1, seed_id).

4) Filtering & tagging
- Privacy filter rules: drop any candidate with > 0.45 probability of containing PII according to pii-detector:v2.
- Tagging taxonomy (example): slice:payment-confusion, intent:refund, modality:text-only, severity:critical|major|minor.

5) Telemetry annotation and ingestion contract
- Telemetry fields (required): probe_id, slice, seed_provenance, synth_tool_version, expected_signal_labels, created_by, creation_ts.
- Runtime capture to request log: probe_id, request_qualifier (shadow/canary/live), model_variant, latency_ms, token_count_input, token_count_output, response_signature_hash, kv-cache-hit(bool), quant-path(label).
- Ingestion frequency: batched ingest to eval-harness once per 6 hours for high-priority slices, daily for exploratory.

6) Eval-harness ingestion and prioritization
- Priority buckets: P0 (customer-facing regression risk), P1 (quality drift observable), P2 (research/coverage).
- Scheduling heuristic (textual): allocate at least 5% of continuous eval budget to rotating P0 probes; maintain a hot-set of 500 P0 probes per model family.

7) Onboarding acceptance checks (sample checklist)
- Coherence: semantic similarity score delta < 0.06 against golden responses on deterministic seed set.
- Functioncall fidelity: 100% structured-output parseability on 200 probes.
- Quant safety: no more than 1.5% of probes show coherence failures attributable to quant path (per quant-profile).
- Latency: 95th percentile latency on target infra < SLO threshold for this slice.
- If any check fails, route to "probe-failure-review" with triage notes.

8) Regression triage hooks and escalation mapping
- Every failing probe must create a triage ticket with: failing-model-variant, observed-signal, golden-sample, recent-deploy-commit, telemetry snapshot link.
- Owner routing: if failure correlates with quant-profile tag -> quant-team; timestamped prefix cache anomalies -> serving-runtime; otherwise -> model-owner.

Probe Manifest template (tabular):
| probe_id | slice | severity | origin (seed/synth) | owner | status | tags | last_verified |
|---------:|:-----:|:--------:|:-------------------:|:-----:|:------:|:----:|:-------------:|
| EX-0001  | payment-confusion | critical | seed | @product-eng | active | payment,context-fade | 2026-02-12 |
| SX-2042  | longcontext-coherence | major | synth:v3 | @applied-ml | review | long-context,kv-cache | 2026-01-20 |

Acceptance criteria and gating rules (compact):
- "Green" if: pass coherence & functioncall & latency checks AND no privacy red flags.
- "Amber" if: minor delta in coherence or latency; schedule human review and increase eval cadence.
- "Red" if: regression causes user-visible incorrect action (e.g., funds transfer error) or privacy exposure risk.

Operational runbook (fast-fail path):
1) Detection: alert from continuous eval or customer report referencing probe_id.
2) Snapshot capture: link to the last 24h request log + model variant.
3) Replay-in-sandbox: run probe against last-good-commit and current-commit with quantized and float paths.
4) Bisect: if behavior diverges, launch model-bisect job (owner: applied-ml).
5) Short-term mitigation: add probe to blocked-hotset and route traffic to fallback variant if P0.
6) Long-term: patch model/quant config or rollback per release policy.

Priority scoring formula (text form):
score = 0.5 * severity_weight + 0.3 * live_traffic_frac_rank + 0.2 * failure_amplification_index
- severity_weight: critical=1.0, major=0.6, minor=0.2
- live_traffic_frac_rank: normalized rank of fraction of similar real traffic (0..1)
- failure_amplification_index: measure of how many downstream tasks would fail if this probe regresses (0..1).

Templates and example snippets
- Probe json example (minified):
{
  "probe_id": "SX-2042",
  "slice": "longcontext-coherence",
  "input": "System: You are a helpful assistant. Conversation:\nUser: Here's my conversation history ... (2000 tokens)\nUser: What did I ask about invoices?",
  "expected_signal_labels": ["mentions-invoice-number", "intent:query"],
  "provenance": "synth:v3",
  "tags": ["long-context","kv-cache-sensitive"]
}

- Ingest CLI (example):
$ rwd-eval ingest --manifest probes/sx-2042.json --priority P0 --env shadow

- Sample YAML for quant gating rule:
quant_profile: q8_hetero_v2
max_coherence_delta: 0.06
fallback_variant: float_v2
rollout_action: block_and_notify

Governance and lifecycle rules:
- Probe ownership must be assigned on creation. Ownership rotates to applied-ml after 90 days of no updates.
- Retirement policy: probes unused in eval runs for 12 months must be archived.
- Sensitive probes (those kept for privacy reasons) are stored in the private probe vault with restricted access and logging.

Onboarding checklist for adding a new probe set into the eval-harness:
- [ ] Slice brief created and approved
- [ ] At least 500 candidate probes generated or 200 for small slices
- [ ] Privacy and legal sign-off if seed-based
- [ ] Telemetry contract file present and validated (schema check pass)
- [ ] Acceptance checks run locally and green on staging
- [ ] Probe manifest entry created and reviewer assigned

Hand-off to regression triage (recommended fields for ticket):
- probe_id, slice, failing_variant, last_good_commit, failing_commit, observed_deltas (coherence/latency/token_counts), attach:request-log-snapshot, owner-recommendation.

Metrics to monitor (baseline set):
- Probe-level pass-rate (daily) by model-variant
- Mean time to detection (probe-originated alerts)
- Time-to-repair (median) for P0 probes
- False-positive rate on automated synthesizer filters

Appendix A: Common pitfalls and mitigations
- Overfitting to synthesized probes: rotate synthesis strategies and include adversarial paraphrase variants.
- Privacy leakage from seed-based probes: always run PII-detector and require legal signoff for customer seeds.
- Probe explosion: use trimming heuristics, dedupe by response-signature-hash.

Appendix B: Roles and responsibilities
- Probe author: creates slice brief and seeds (product / ML writer).
- Synthesizer owner: maintains generation tools and improves filters (applied-ml).
- Probe steward: maintains manifest, triage queue, and release gating (platform-qa).
- Triage owner: first responder for failing probes (oncall applied-ml engineer).

Appendix C: Example escalation matrix (brief)
- P0 failure during business hours: page oncall applied-ml -> 30 min SLA to acknowledge -> 2 hours to mitigation plan.
- P1: ticket in triage board, 48h review commitment.
- P2: batched review in weekly probe stewardship meeting.

Links and references:
- Eval Harness ingestion spec: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/evaluation-asset-registry-and-service-contract-2026
- Quant profile playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024
- Regression triage runbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/field-eval-fast-path-and-rollback-playbook-2025

If you are adding a new slice, ping @applied-ml on Slack with the slice brief and draft manifest. For questions about tooling, contact the Synthesizer owner (Samir Patel).
